objective: Evaluate the effectiveness of the Nucleus device in reducing motion artifacts during heart rate monitoring during 30 minutes of moderate-intensity cycling
independent_variables: Nucleus device with motion artifact reduction
standard photoplethysmographic sensor without motion artifact reduction
controls: arm movement in a controlled manner to simulate real-world exercise conditions
baseline: RMSE of heart rate monitoring using a standard photoplethysmographic sensor without motion artifact reduction
procedure: Recruit 20 healthy subjects with no history of cardiovascular disease
Instruct subjects to perform 30 minutes of moderate-intensity cycling on a controlled ergometer
Measure RMSE of heart rate monitoring using both the Nucleus device and the standard photoplethysmographic sensor
Repeat the experiment with the subject's arm moved in a controlled manner to simulate real-world exercise conditions
expected_result: A 25% decrease in RMSE of heart rate monitoring using the Nucleus device compared to the standard photoplethysmographic sensor
falsification_condition: If the RMSE of heart rate monitoring using the Nucleus device is not significantly lower than the baseline (p < 0.05) after 30 minutes of moderate-intensity cycling
sample_requirements: 20 healthy subjects with no history of cardiovascular disease
safety_constraints: Ensure that subjects are not experiencing any discomfort or pain during the experiment
information_gain: The effectiveness of the Nucleus device in reducing motion artifacts during heart rate monitoring during 30 minutes of moderate-intensity cycling
